name: FL-19
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's R+14 partisan lean keeps the open Southwest Florida seat in Republican hands
Massive fundraising gap: Schwartzel has raised about $2.1M versus under $60K for Arias
Prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 94%
Open seat after Donalds' retirement removes incumbent advantage, but no polling shows competition
model.rationale: The R+14 lean of this open seat, a fundraising gap of roughly $2.0 million versus $58 thousand, and prediction markets pricing the Republican at about 94% all point to a comfortable Republican hold; with no public polling or expert ratings available, uncertainty stays elevated, but the structural evidence is one-sided.
model.watch: Any public polling showing the Democrat within single digits, or a Democratic national wave exceeding historical norms, would be the main signals of a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Byron Donalds (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Byron Donalds' retirement to run for governor leaves this heavily Republican Southwest Florida seat open, but the district's R+14 partisan lean keeps it firmly in the Republican column. Jim Schwartzel has raised more than two million dollars for the Republican side, while Democrat Victor Arias has raised under sixty thousand, a gap of roughly thirty-five to one that leaves Democrats with little means to compete.

No public polling covers the general election and no expert ratings track the race, so the outlook rests on the district's fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price the Republican at about ninety-four percent. An open seat removes the incumbent's personal vote, but the partisan baseline in this district has historically absorbed such swings. A Republican win by roughly fifteen points is the expected outcome, with a Democratic victory possible only in an extreme wave scenario.
